update.method: The anger ledger's section M (AN-H1 to AN-H5) read outward by guide v2 (#2168). Correction (rule 77, a verse fitted to a line): Judg 14:19 taken out of 'The Spirit of God comes with anger' in 10.13 Other parties; Samson's hot anger given its own ground in the passage (Judg 14:15-20, outwitted through his wife) under What it rises at. 2Ki 3:27, held in 10.13 since the anger strand, read with 3:18 and 3:26 and the other 'wrath came upon' verses (qesep, H7110A; 2Ch 32:25-26): the bearer stated as open. Found by reading outward: anger in the body, the teeth (a set-based pull of the gnashing words H2786, G1031, G1030). Woven: 10.13 v13 (Being outwitted through someone close; new subsection Anger in the body; the Spirit bullet corrected; Once, with no bearer named; Rev 18:3; the held line removed), 10.12 v15 (Eze 21:15), 10.10 v33 (Samson's wife: fear passed on as pressure), Ch 2 v28 (weeping and gnashing of teeth, Luk 13:28), Ch 12 v26 (Num 20:13). AN-H1 (withdrawn 2026-10-01), the pilot rows, the unit 2 revisit-note verses and Rom 13:5 were found already told; AN-H3 stays with signpost #1893; AN-H5 data.

new.text: Samson's hot anger has its ground in being outwitted through his wife; the Spirit's rushing goes with the striking at Ashkelon
new.beyond_text: separates the two parts of Judg 14:19 by the passage's own ground (14:16-18)

new.text: Anger shows in the body, and the verses see it in the teeth: the angry, the plotter, the enraged hearers, gloating enemies and mockers gnash their teeth
new.beyond_text: gathers the gnashing verses as anger seen in the body

new.text: Job pictures God's anger, as he feels it under it, as gnashing of teeth
new.beyond_text: reads Job 16:9 as the sufferer's view of God's anger

new.text: In 2 Kings 3:27 the wrath has no bearer named and no breach before it, and the verse leaves open whose wrath it was
new.beyond_text: compares the verse with the other 'wrath came upon' verses, where a breach comes first

new.text: In Ezekiel 21:15 the melting heart is what the sword is given for
new.beyond_text: reads the purpose clause as fear aimed at the heart

new.text: Fear laid on Samson's wife became the weeping she laid on him to get his secret
new.beyond_text: joins the threat (14:15) to the tears and pressure (14:16-17)

new.text: At the judgment the shut-out weep and gnash their teeth at a sight: others inside, themselves outside
new.beyond_text: reads Luke's 'when you see' as the moment of the weeping and gnashing
